speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming your symptoms. To better understand your condition, can you tell me if you experience any nausea, vomiting, or hearing loss alongside the vertigo?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is a very short duration for true vertigo; does the spinning sensation recur with head movement now, and did you notice any new weakness, slurred speech, or double vision?

REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike maneuver
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain (if symptoms are recurrent or atypical)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dix-Hallpike Manoeuvre: Positive, inducing nystagmus and reproducing patient's symptoms of vertigo when head is turned to the left and laid back. Head Imaging: Normal, with no evidence of stroke or masses.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness. I am scared this situation could become urgent and I need the most appropriate final answer immediately. Please do not wait too long before committing to a next step.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The brief duration of your symptoms and their sudden onset without neurological deficits strongly suggest this condition. Please return to the clinic within 24 hours for a Dix-Hallpike maneuver and canalith repositioning procedure to resolve the issue.
